summary: Maurine Stuart was a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at the University of Manitoba (~1940–1944) and trained under traditional teachers Hakuun Yasutani (~1965–1973) and Eido Tai Shimano (~1970–1979).

Maurizio Taddei worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was a professor at the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente (attested 1994) and Director of the Editorial Committee at the Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente (~1996–2000).

Mauro Maggi specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology, earning his doctorate from the University of Naples "L'Orientale." He held posts at the University of Hamburg (1990), Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2018), and directed the Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente.

Mavis L. Fenn studied at the University of Winnipeg, University of Calgary, and McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen. In Buddhist and religious studies, she held posts at United College (~2005–2006) and the University of Waterloo (attested 2016) as Professor and Department Chair.

Max Deeg works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, completing his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg. He served as Head of the School of Religious and Theological Studies at Cardiff University (attested 2010–2021).

Max Leopold Margolis was a linguistics and religious studies scholar who studied at Columbia University (~1889–1891). He held positions at Columbia (~1891–1892), UC Berkeley (~1897–1905), and Dropsie College for Hebrew and Cognate Learning (~1909–1932).
Max Lindenau was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch, concluding his studies in 1913.

Max Oidtmann is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard University under Mark C. Elliott, later holding a post at Georgetown University (~2014).

Max Walleser worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held a post at Heidelberg University (~1908–1937) and founded both the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the Institut für Buddhismus-Kunde.
Maxime Kaltenmark was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Paris and the École Pratique des Hautes Études from ~1957 to 1979.
McDougal is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts (Research) at the University of Sydney, supervised by Geoffrey Samuel and Mark Allon.

McKim Marriott was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago (~1948–1953). He served as professor of anthropology and social sciences at the University of Chicago from ~1957 to 1998.

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Nanjing University. In 2008, he held teaching posts at the University of Colombo and other Sri Lankan institutions.
Megan Bryson works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She studied at Stanford University and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).
Megumu Honda is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Paul Tedesco and Rulon Wells. Honda held a professorship at Doho University (attested 1996).
Mei Ching Hsuan is a Tibetology scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2009), where she studied under Peter Schwieger and Dieter Schuh.
Meiji Yamada is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962). He subsequently held a professorship there, attested in 1963 and 2007.
Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts from Fo Guang University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin.

Melissa R. Kerin works in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter, and held a professorship at Washington and Lee University (attested 2015).

Melvyn C. Goldstein is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. After studying at the University of Michigan and completing his PhD at the University of Washington, he became a professor at Case Western Reserve University (~1968).
